questions.question_text:
RECALL AND CONNECT 1:
a) What is thermal expansion in relation to climate change?
b) What are ice cores and how have they advanced knowledge about climate change?

marking_scheme.rubric: AO1 and AO2: Answer cross-topic questions on climate change.
keywords_required: a) As the Earth's oceans warm due to climate change, the water expands, causing sea levels to rise.
b) Ice cores are cylinders of ice drilled from ice sheets/glaciers.
They trap air bubbles from thousands of years ago, allowing scientists to measure past atmospheric carbon dioxide levels and temperatures.

questions.question_text: Sketch a diagram to explain why Antarctica experiences 24 hours of sunlight at certain times of the year.

marking_scheme.rubric: AO1 and AO2: Diagram showing the Earth's tilt and its effect on polar sunlight.
keywords_required: Diagram must show the Earth tilted on its axis (23.5 degrees).
Sun's rays pointing towards the Earth.
During the Southern Hemisphere's summer, the South Pole is tilted towards the Sun.
Because of this tilt, areas within the Antarctic Circle remain exposed to sunlight continuously as the Earth rotates.
Clear labels (Earth's axis, Sun's rays, South Pole).

questions.question_text: Sketch a diagram to show why the air above Antarctica is usually cold and dry.

marking_scheme.rubric: AO1 and AO2: Diagram showing atmospheric circulation at the poles.
keywords_required: Diagram showing descending cold air at the South Pole (high pressure).
Cold air holds very little moisture, hence it is dry.
The white ice sheet has a high albedo, reflecting most of the sun's incoming solar radiation (insolation).
Low angle of the sun means heat is spread over a larger area.
Labels indicating descending air, high albedo, and high atmospheric pressure.
